utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, to whom is this document addressed?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: This document is addressed to the Command of the El Mudjahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And what is the purpose of this particular order?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't know the purpose of this order, but this order was an order that was not made for anyone in particular. This was the first item in the preparations for the offensive operations which were part of Operation Farz.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But, sir, the document is titled "Order for Intelligence Support," and I was wondering if you could tell us what the purpose of an order for intelligence support would be.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: The purpose of an order of this kind is to let all the units know about the enemy strength and what they might expect in the course of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, why did you provide this information to the Command of the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: This information was forwarded by my commander, not myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Your Honour, I would ask that this document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that: You have just told us, sir, that this document was signed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in fact you have just told us that the initials "HI," they are your initials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is the significance of those initials, sir? What do they mean to the reader?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reader knows who the author of the text is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are not just the signatory to the document, but you are also the author of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So in fact the content of the document is your brainchild?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then why are you not able to tell us why you provided this information to the El Mujahedin Command, detachment command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I was ordered to provide this information to the El Mudjahedin Detachment, and this information was meant for all the units in the 35th Division. If you -- look, can I give you a more extensive explanation or do you just want me to give you an answer to your question and that's it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want an answer to my question, that's it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information was drafted for all the units participating in the attack, not for just one unit. And since this unit did not get it, the commander ordered me to write it and to send it to them, too, and then I put the name of Mr. Hasanagic underneath and I signed it for him. It says "for Hasanagic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that, but the document was drafted by you. You had the information that had to go into the document, number one. Now, let me ask you another question. Forget about the content. Now, this unit to which you were sending this order, was it a unit of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I considered that it was not, and that is why I did not send it to them while I was sending it to everybody else. And then I received an order later on to send it to them as well, and that's why I did it. It was done afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So at this time when you sent this order, you became aware that this is now a unit of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what you said. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking you the question. I'm not saying, I'm asking you. Now when you were ordered to send this order, did you then at that time become aware of the fact that this unit is a unit of the 35th Division; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A few minutes ago, when you were being asked whether this unit is a unit of the 35th Division, you then knew that it was a unit of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're talking about different time periods. We were talking about spring a little while ago, and now we're talking about a different time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking you the question. A few minutes ago, when you were asked the question, you knew that in this time period on the 24th of August, 1995, the El Mudjahedin Detachment was a unit of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me say that again. I didn't know that. I don't know it now. But this was an indication, if I received an order to send this kind of a report, that this was a possibility. You asked me yes or no, and I really didn't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't think I understand your answer, sir. Let me make myself clear. I'm asking you a question that a few minutes ago, when you were asked whether the El Mudjahedin Detachment was a unit of the 35th Division, you knew that as of the 24th of August, 1995, you had been given instructions to send the El Mudjahedin Detachment this order because you were then informed that the El Mudjahedin Detachment was a unit of the 35th Division? Is that correct or not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not correct. I don't know how this misunderstanding occurred. It was the end of the war, and I still didn't know that the El Mudjahedin Detachment had ever been part of the 35th Division. But you asked me a different thing a while ago, the fact that I knew that it was part of the 35th Division. This order wouldn't have gone to them separately and everybody else, and the order wouldn't have the same significance, because when I send my own reports, I address it to whoever, I don't send it to units separately. I send it to a staff, and then the staff produces combat documents, because item 1 is my item in all combat reports. Why this was sent to them separately is not something that I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Who ordered you to send the order also to the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably the commander. Who else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would ask now that this document be tendered into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And I just want to do clarify one point.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 556.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In the exchange between Your Honour and the witness, he referred to the spring.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "the spring," are you referring to a military operation or something else?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the military operation Proljece. We discussed it a while ago, and the question was whether I knew that this military unit was part of the 35th Division or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, sir. Sir, I want to talk further about the Farz operation. Do you know if prisoners of war were taken during that particular operation?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And when did you become aware that prisoners of war were taken during that particular operation?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date. I did receive a report, though, to the effect that men had been taken during the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And from whom did you receive this report, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: From my assistant. He was at the forward command post at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Which forward command post was he at, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Klek, 777.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And which -- and where were you when you received this report, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where I was. During the operation itself, the 35th Division had five or six different forward command posts which changed as the line shifted. I can't remember exactly where it was that I was caught by these developments. Maybe in Zavidovici or elsewhere. It was probably the second or third forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And when you say "second or third command post," do those two command posts have names?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: You see, these command posts -- yes, they did have names, and they were set up as the situation required. We couldn't know how far we would get. We couldn't know what would happen. We tried to adapt to the situation as it evolved and as we made progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, what were the names of the second and third command posts?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Second, third nomenclature. The second and third forward command post was in Babylon [as interpreted], and the next day we moved to Hajderovici. Then after that, we went to the Blizna area. And then later, it was Maglaj. There were at least four, as far as I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And now returning to the prisoners of war, do you recall how many prisoners of war were taken?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't, but it was a large number, 50, 60. I really have no idea. It was a large number, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, where were these prisoners of war captured?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, they were captured in the Kesten area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And who captured these prisoners, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, whether it was the 1st or the 5th Battalion, but I know that it was a battalion from the Gostovici area. It was more about areas for us. I remembered areas rather than numbers, numerical designations, since military units were often reshaped, reorganised. I even knew the commander of the unit from that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, this -- the battalion which captured these prisoners, which brigade was it a part of?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Can I just correct something that I said earlier on? The battalion, yes, the battalion, the 3rd or the 5th, or rather a company of the 3rd or the 5th Battalion, a company of one of these battalions, if I can just amend what I said earlier. It wasn't the entire battalion that captured these people. It was a single company. They were part of the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the 328th Brigade, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Husein Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, do you know the name of the commander of the unit or in this case the company that captured these particular prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I later learned his name. I knew him from the early days, when the army had not been organised yet. We had those patriotic forces, as we called them. His last name was Sogolj. I do know his nickname, but I don't know his real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, who is the -- and you've referred to the 3rd or the 5th -- well, the 3rd or the 5th Battalion. Who were the commanders of the 3rd and the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I no longer remember. You said the 3rd, and if you could just please -- I may have made a mistake. The 2nd or the 5th Battalion, the 2nd or the 5th, these two had to do with Gostovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, do you know the name of the commander of the 2nd Battalion, by any chance? And if you don't recall, just tell me you don't know.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now, when you found out about the capture of these prisoners, do you know in whose custody they were?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, but I do know that they were captured by one of these battalions. I don't know what happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And what did you do with the information that you received concerning these prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: As soon as I received the information, I didn't process it or embellish it. I just submitted this to my superior command in the form in which I had received it, which means I sent it on to the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And to whom in the corps did you send this?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: The same person that I was sending all other documents to, assistant commander for Intelligence of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, again, for clarification, who would this be?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Edin Husic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Did you report this information to your other superior, the commander of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I believe I said this once already. All the information received by the corps was always submitted to the division commander, at least as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what happened to these prisoners after their capture?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I certainly don't. I did hear something later on, but this is something that I heard. Therefore, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you heard?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I heard that the Arabs took them away from this detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And from whom did you hear this, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't even remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And do you recall when you --

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: But this wasn't on the record. I wasn't told officially, however, but I don't know. I heard one, two, or three days later. I really don't know. You see, at the time we had a lot of different commitments, responsibilities, other business. The only way for me to receive information was by phone or through a report, or we were in the mountains. Access was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, you said: "I heard one, two, or three days later." What are you referring to when you say "one, two, or three days later"; after what?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: After receiving the report. I don't actually know when it was that I heard this. I simply can't remember when I heard it. I can't even remember what the report looked like that I received. I don't even know what it says. I really don't know. I can't remember the report. Did I look at it? Did I not? And I don't have any documents available to me to jog my memory or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, you've referred to a report. Does this report refer to the prisoners being in the custody of the Arabs?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't know. The first time around, you asked me when I heard about this, and I said I received a report from the forward command post. I merely rephrased the report a little and sent it on to the corps, but I don't remember the document. It was such a long time ago, I don't know what it said, but I do remember there were a large number of captured enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection. The witness just answered precisely what he had said earlier on. He had heard about prisoners, captured soldiers, and now this was a leading question as to the prisoners being in the custody of the Arabs. The witness never said anything about the report actually indicating that. This is a leading question, and I do believe that we should avoid this sort of practice in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was simply -- the witness had answered, "After receiving the report," and I wanted to clarify the content of the report. I take my learned friend's suggestion on board. Perhaps I could have rephrased that question in a less leading way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, did you hear anything further about what happened to these prisoners after they fell into the custody of the Arabs?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No. If I may just add something. Had the situation been different, had we not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, again a leading question. This witness is being consistently and adamantly led on the issue of these prisoners being held in the custody of some Arabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Madam Vidovic, if you look at page 55, line 16, the witness said -- I beg your pardon, it's line 17: "I heard that the Arabs took them away from this detachment." And I've got this question which I want to actually still follow with the witness, and I'm not quite sure whether that doesn't mean that, in fact, they got into the custody of the Arabs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is precisely why I'm objecting. That is the purpose of my objection, what you have just stated. The witness says he heard about that, but he doesn't know what became of them later, and how could he?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, but now your objection is shifting. Your objection was that he's being led on the question of the prisoners of war being in the custody of the Arabs. Now you want to say how is he supposed to know what happened to them later, and that's a different mission. I'm still on the one, trying to explain to you why it is being suggested that they were in the hands of the Arabs, because the witness has said so himself at line 17 of page 55.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said he had heard that they were being held by the Arabs, and now he's being led on the following: It is being put to him what became of those people after they left the Arabs. The witness just heard something, and then how would he know? Yes, for me, it's definitely impossible for him to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why couldn't he hear also what became of them, and if he heard what became of them, he would say he heard what became of them, and if he didn't hear, he would say he didn't hear. This is the problem that, in this Tribunal, hearsay evidence is accepted and we would have stopped this earlier, but now if you accept that he could hear that the Arabs took them, then you must accept that he could also hear what became of them. And let's hear what he's got to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us if you heard what happened to the Arabs -- excuse me, what happened to the prisoners after the Arabs took them away?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know what became of them. Even what I've said, I just heard it. I was physically elsewhere altogether. If you get that map, I was somewhere along the road to Maglaj, and this happened somewhere along the road to Banovici, which is a different area, the road to Vozuca. This is an entirely different area, the distance being 30 or more kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir. Sir, when did you leave the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Sorry, did Your Honours want to ask a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I thought it was a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I have just one question, and that was going to be my last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought so too. Okay, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, you may answer that question. When did you leave the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I was demobilised in June 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. No further questions, Your Honour, from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Menon. We will take a break at this time and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examination by Madam Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hajrulahovic. I'm Vasvija Vidovic. I'll be asking you today on behalf of General Delic's Defence. The nature of cross-examination is such that most frequently you will be able to answer "yes" or "no." However, if at times you should find it necessary to provide additional explanations, by all means, please do so. Further, I would like to ask you to speak slowly and make a pause between my questions and your answers, given the fact that we have problems with the interpretation and recording the actual words being said. Do you understand me, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Hajderhodzic, before the war you used to work as a project manager; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You did not complete any military schools or anything like that; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You completed your -- the regular compulsory military term with the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You left the JNA with the rank of sergeant; yes?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Before the war, I mean before the war, you did not take any specialised courses in intelligence, did you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Before the war, you never did anything that had anything at all to do with intelligence, did you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Therefore, you had neither the training required to do that sort of job nor any experience in intelligence work; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, but I was a member of the Reconnaissance and Sabotage Unit, a reserve unit, which was attached to the Zavidovici Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Before the war?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you agree that the fact that you were a member of this reconnaissance unit, reconnaissance squad, did not necessarily endow you with any technical knowledge, such as is required for any high-ranking positions in the intelligence field?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Being assistant commander of the division commander for Intelligence implied that the incumbent would have completed a military academy of some kind, would have some sort of experience and also hold the rank of at least a colonel in the army; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't know this for a fact, but it sounds right. I assume you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You don't even know what the criteria would have been for someone to become an assistant commander for Intelligence in an organised army; right? Today, you answered some questions about the job of an intelligence officer and the job of someone involved in military security. You first answered questions by the OTP, and then you were asked a question by the Presiding Judge, His Honour Moloto. You said that you believed the job of an intelligence officer to be -- of a security officer to be this: To control everything that was going on in the area of responsibility of the unit to which you belonged. You remember that you said that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And you said, "This is my personal position," and this is indeed your personal opinion, because you will agree, will you not, the BH Army adopted its own rules and regulations at the beginning of the war; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that there was a rule governing the work of the Security Service?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about that, but I did not read it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes. You did not read it, did you?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: There was also a rule governing the work of the military police. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you agree that these regulations also defined the responsibilities of the Ministry of the Interior in the war?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And you agree that you did not spend any time reading or analysing those rules and regulations?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: By all means, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Therefore, when you speak of responsibility, these are your assumptions about what the rules actually say, but you don't know it for a fact?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Very well. Now I wish to ask you something, and I believe you might know this, and it's about the following context. It's about the context of events that you discussed yesterday in the locality of Zavidovici. You spent time there, as far as I understand, both in 1994 and 1995, even 1993. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You provided a very detailed account of the circumstances under which various units were set up in 1993, after the military authorities had taken the decision to establish the corps. You made a statement to the OTP, to their investigators. First of all, do you recall making a statement like that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you remember making a statement in April 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the witness mumbles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Let me invoke a particular portion of your testimony. This is 938515. This is a tape. This is page 5 of the Bosnian translation of the transcript and page 6 of the English. Witness, I can read the relevant portion out to you. If necessary, I can point out to you what you said. It's a small portion of your own statement. You answered the investigator's question in the following way: "Well, there, I'm telling you again, you have units comprising men who never thought they would be soldiers. These are men who were taken away from their fruit tree gardens or factories yesterday, wherever they used to work, furniture factories, and we had to make soldiers out of these people." Do you remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: To the investigator, full stop. Do you accept that in Zavidovici, the army took quite long to establish itself, longer than in Tuzla and Sarajevo, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I certainly agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: The soldiers were untrained and they had to be organised; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: What is peculiar to the Zavidovici area is this: Zavidovici, because of the clashes with the HVO in 1993 and all the way until the Washington Agreement, had been cut off from Zenica; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Again, I wish to quote a portion of your statement. It's a brief one, the statement that you gave to the investigators. Your Honours, again the reference for the tape is 9388A. The page is 7 in the Bosnian and 9 and 10 in the English. You described the situation in Zavidovici in the following way: "We literally stayed behind in Zavidovici, and the 3rd Corps, or units of the 3rd Corps, were cut off, literally. They had no physical contact with the Command." So this situation prevailed until the time the Washington Agreement was reached; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this situation, where military units were isolated from the Command of the 3rd Corps, resulted in a strong influence being exerted on life in the area, including the army, by local civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: This influence was exerted because the support for the army depended on the civilian authorities; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In your testimony today, you mentioned the establishment of the Bosna Operations Group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the establishment of the Bosna Operations Group was done because of the particular influence on the part of the local Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the details, but I assume that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Let me ask you the following: Do you agree with me -- let us put aside the party for the moment -- that the local politicians and businessmen exerted substantial influence on the establishment of military units?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Let me give you an example. The 320th Brigade, this brigade was set up at the request of the local politicians, at their exclusive request?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You described this situation in detail for the benefit of the investigators, but let me now show you once again an excerpt, because I believe that this is relevant, and that I believe you can explain to us some issues here. You said, I'm referring now to tape 9388B, page 3 and 4 in the Bosnian version, and that's pages 4 and 5 in the English version, you said: "Politics tried to get involved in military matters. The 318th Brigade had such people. Some of the people from the 318th Brigade would not allow that, and we wanted that if the politics had anything to add or subtract, let the politicians do that through our superior command. And that was the proper position, and it was clear to them that this was a proper position. That is why a large part of the Command of the 318th Brigade left to go to some other military [Realtime transcript read in error "other formation"] formation." And you also said that the division -- or rather that the politicians in Zavidovici insisted that they should decide where the division should have its headquarters once it was established; is that so? Is this correct? Did you, in fact, say so to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we perhaps have a correction to the English transcript, where another military formation is mentioned? The term "military" is not in the transcript. It has not been interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me try and clarify that through a question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do that, Madam Vidovic, can you please direct us clearly, on the English, what you are quoting from, because I've been looking at this page that is displayed here to try and find out what is it you are talking about, and I am completely lost. Can we just check whether the English page that we have is the same page that we are supposed to be reading from?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am talking about the statement this witness gave to the OTP investigators. That's the tape. I don't know whether you have it in front of you. But if you do, that's at 9388B, pages 3 and 4 in the Bosnian version, 4 and 5 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do I find 9388B?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can show D523 if you want to see this part of his statement. That's D -- can we please have D? Your Honours, let me just check whether there has been some misunderstanding or misinterpretation. I am referring to the statement that this witness gave to the OTP investigators, and if necessary I can always -- we have those excerpts in the system, but if I'm quoting from them, I always have this feeling that we're wasting our time. But if it's necessary, I can have them brought up to our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, okay, I'm with you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, we were talking about the way in which brigades were set up in the Zavidovici area. Did I understand you correctly that in 1994, in that area, there was a brigade, 318th Brigade, that was quite successful and disciplined?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my opinion, and I still have this opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are asked to speak into the microphone, please. The interpreters don't hear you. Please speak into the microphone. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yet despite that, the local politicians demanded that another brigade be set up that would obey their orders, and it was set up?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In your statement to the investigators, the OTP investigators asked you in detail about Asim Camdzic's unit. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You said that you did not know under whose command that unit was in 1994 and 1995, despite the fact that formally speaking, it was a part of the army structure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Let me now stay with this unit for a moment. Do you agree that this was a unit with a pronounced religious bent; it carried religious insignia instead of the army insignia, it emulated the Arabs? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: It did not really fit into the command-and-control system?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: From my point of view, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: It obeyed the orders that came from outside of the BH Army; that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: That's what I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You told the investigators that this was a reconnaissance and sabotage-type unit; as such, it should have been under your personal command. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yet it wasn't?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In your evidence, you said that the Bosna Operations Group became the 35th Division in early 1995; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the 35th Division inherited all the problems of this kind that we discussed related to command and control from OG Bosna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Furthermore, it set up the various sections and sectors in the Command, but in essence it had a lot of untrained personnel holding officer positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will be referring again to the statement this witness gave to the Prosecutor, to the OTP investigators. That's at 9389B, that's the reference to the tape, page 2 both in the English and in the Bosnian versions, and I will quote just a little portion thereof, if the witness is able to recall having said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Witness, you said in this section: "I have to say something that might not really be, since there were some -- there was some hesitation on your part, there was some amateurs such as myself, quite a few of us."

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, these are the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: So it is a fact that in the 35th Division, the most responsible positions, positions involving the highest level of responsibility, were held by untrained personnel?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were only two or three people who were graduates of military schools, and they held appropriate ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And those amateurs performed important tasks in the sphere of military security?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Intelligence?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: It is correct that the 3rd Corps tried to organise courses, or rather it did organise courses, in order to improve the knowledge of those officers; am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: The corps organised, in particular, training for intelligence officers in order for them to be able to draft the regular reports, intelligence reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And you took this course?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Not that one. I took another one, the one in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Fine, fine. But you attended this course that provided you with some knowledge that enabled you to draft those intelligence reports?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a bit broader, but, yes, in principle, that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In your evidence, you explained that it was your duty to gather intelligence about the enemy, or the aggressor as you called them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: That means that you were to gather intelligence about the Republika Srpska Army, their strength, disposition, capabilities, plans?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You did that as best you could?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You had some makeshift ham radio equipment to intercept the communications of the Republika Srpska Army personnel?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But prisoners of war were a source of information for you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: They should have been, but in our case they were not because we didn't learn anything in particular from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Fine, fine, yes, but now I'm speaking in general, when we're talking about sources of intelligence.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But I will go back to this specific situation. We'll deal with that in detail. The intelligence organ in your division where you were the assistant did not have equipment for its work?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I mean cameras, other photographic equipment, recorders, movie cameras, night vision equipment; you did not have that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You did not have people who would be able to use that equipment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, probably, even if we -- or rather if we had this equipment, we may have found people who would have been able to operate this equipment, but we didn't have the equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I suppose that you relied on the intelligence sources that you could obtain, given your technical capabilities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Let me now dwell briefly on the Command of the 35th Division. Do you agree with me that in 1995, interpersonal relations in the 35th Division Command were very bad?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, people were not on the best of terms. I don't know any specific examples, but the situation was quite bad. You could feel it. I was on good terms with everyone, but many things were left unclear and that forced people to -- that made you suspect that not everything was right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm asking you this question on the basis of your conversations with the OTP investigators, the interview with them. And could you tell me, is it true that the chief of Staff was not on speaking terms with the division commander, that they would not talk to each other for a month, for instance?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether they were on speaking terms or not, but their relationship was very tense, very, very, very tense. It is difficult for me to comment on those relations, because they were my superior officers, but it is true that it was tense. It was not something that I would have expected, so I'm now just speaking from my own point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you something. Is it true that the chief of Staff would not attend the briefings for a month at all, that he was just not physically there?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: The relations between Samir Hamdzic, the assistant commander for logistics, and the commander were also bad?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And finally the relations between the assistant commander for Security and the commander were also bad; is that true?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness please be shown Exhibit 455.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 455, 455.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at page 1. This is a document produced by the Command of the 35th Division, the 21st of July, 1995. This is a report, a regular combat report or a daily combat report, being sent to the Operations Centre of the 3rd Corps. If the witness could please look at the last page of this document. Your Honours, page 7 in the English, the last page. Sir, could you please look at the section that talks about the security situation. You testified today about your contact with the prisoners in the El Mudjahid Detachment. Can you read the part that says "typical problems"? Can you agree that this portion of the document clearly says that there is a problem with documents and the fact that there is no access to prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please go back to page 1 of this document. If we could please have item 3, "Morale."

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Please read what it says under "(a)," "Combat Morale." Before I ask you a question about morale, let me ask you this: If I look at the portion in reference to security, it is clear that there is reference here to instructions from the 3rd Corps based on which one was supposed to report on POWs; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You know about those instructions; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: All right. You see this bit on page 3 that says there is a problem, right, and do you agree about morale, that it says they are reporting on their success and how this is affecting the morale? The El Mujahid unit has great influence on the combat morale and security with their morale and way of life they have become a role model to our soldiers." Now, let me ask you this: How do you explain the fact that the commander signs a document where you have part of the Command Staff saying this, and then in the morale section the other part of the morale staff? Does that have to do with the disrupted relations inside the Command, which is what I've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, most certainly you are on the right track there. This is about something, and let me clarify, if I may. What affected appointments to the Division Command was, among other things, politics. Assistant commander for Morale, for example, was, as a rule, a political appointment, and hence the assessment. And I have to repeat what I've already said in that report. The commander tried to give unlimited freedom to all bodies within the division, freedom in their work. There were a lot of untrained people, amateurs. Some knew their job, some just thought they knew their job but didn't. The commander tried to lend equal support to everyone, and he did not wish to alter or amend their portions of the report. He would just let it be, fearing possible clashes with other people, and that is why this contradiction arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you the following in the most direct way possible: Mr. Hasanagic [as interpreted], did you on the 21st of July tell your own story, the situation that you witnessed involving those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I don't think that I did. Actually, I can't really say anything. You know why I can't say anything? I can't say anything because I took my notebook. I don't have a single document that would allow me to say anything, to go through it, to jog my memory. It would be dishonest of me to say anything at all that I can't back with a document, something that I can't claim. I went back to my notebook, and the notebook literally reads: "I know nothing." At the time that operations were underway, we had a lot on our plate. I know that I followed my new job at the time. I don't even know what the first time was that we met after that. We all did our different jobs in different places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'll return to that question in some detail at a later stage. However, about this, there's something else I want to ask you. Do you remember that it would be an exceptionally strange idea to use people who are mistreating prisoners as some sort of a role model for morale? How would you find the idea, personally?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, let me tell you. I, for one, couldn't even believe there was anything like that happening, and that's why I could hardly wait to leave that room and that sort of thing. But I see this document now. I didn't have a chance to see too many combat reports, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Very well, very well. Let me dwell on the relations that we spoke about, we can put this document away, relations between the commander of the 35th Division and other people. Sir, is it true that the relations between him and the commander of the 328th Division, Mr. Zilkic, were also compromised to a large extent?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: When you made your statement to the investigator, you spoke about Mr. Zilkic, Mr. Zilkic being the commander of the 328th Brigade. That is the person we are talking about; right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: When you made your statement to the investigator in April 2007, you said that you, too, had certain problems with Zilkic because he was using intelligence officers in a way that ran counter to regulations, and he was using intelligence officers for all sorts of other tasks and assignments that they weren't meant to be used for; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You described Mr. Hasanagic today and his relationship with you, the way he treated you, the way he treated reporting. You spoke in great detail about this as well to the investigators of the OTP, did you not? And here I invoke page 9389B -- tape, I'm sorry, tape, tape 9389B, page 5 of the Bosnian and pages 6 and 7 of the English. You say: "I had no problems with my commander. Really, he never asked a single question. Perhaps he had respect for my age, but the fact remains is that he never asked a thing about the reports." What I infer from this and what I want to ask you as well -- first of all, did I quote you correctly?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Therefore, I infer based on this that the division commander was not really strict. Reports could be written but weren't necessarily always written. That is my inference. Right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: May I clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Certainly, sir. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: You see, I'd previously worked with the 318th Brigade. It was my responsibility to write the reports there. That was a long time ago. The commander of the 318th Brigade at the time wanted to have a hand in how I was producing my reports. There were some awful misunderstandings and so on and so forth. When I came to the division, Mr. Hasanagic was adamant that the report should be written, but he didn't meddle, he didn't interfere. He wanted reports to be written. He wanted to eventually be shown these reports. But he never tried to affect in any way what the substance of my reports would be. It wasn't about the reports being written or not being written. Sometimes reports were not written, but then there would be an intervention by the assistant commander for Intelligence of the 3rd Corps, and that was a bad situation for me, because he was the person that the report would eventually be forwarded to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But do you agree that your superior, in a technical sense, Mr. Husic, did not know what was going on on the ground unless you informed him in writing; would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you accept the fact that a commander who works on the ground has more of an insight into what's going on?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's certainly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you accept that it was his responsibility to make sure that everything was included in the reports that was of relevance in his area?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I definitely agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: All right. I will now briefly dwell on interpersonal relations within the division. What prompts this question is something you said a while ago. You said that politics had a degree of influence on certain people, on certain appointments, rather. You mentioned the post of assistant commander for Morale. Am I right to believe that the reason for the poor state of interpersonal relations in the division was the rift in the division and in the brigades brought about by the overbearing influence of local politicians and certain religious leaders? Could I put it that way?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you certainly could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: That is because certain individuals from the army accepted this influence, put up with this influence, whereas some others refused to; could I put it that way?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we show the witness Exhibit 509. 509.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Witness, just to let you know immediately, I don't expect you to comment on how this document was produced. I will ask you about certain facts stated in this document. First of all, do you agree that this is a document produced by the security department of the 3rd Corps, the date being the 12th of August, 1995, and the header being "Relations in the Area of Responsibility of the 35th Division"? I assume you are familiar with these relations, and that is precisely why I would like to ask you a number of questions about this. First of all, can you please read to yourself the first paragraph, the long one, if you can, please. I don't know if you've seen this document or not.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you about some facts stated therein. The document talks about civilian bodies expressing their distrust for the Division Command, which has become a place where people gather who are in inter-ethnic marriages and various kinds of merchants. "Inter-ethnic marriages," what does that mean? Marriage between a Muslim and a non-Muslim, is that what it's a reference to?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Is it true that there was this lack of trust, distrust of the Division Command?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were misgivings, mistrust, precisely for these reasons: We had, in our composition, people not just with inter-ethnic marriages but people who were of different ethnicities themselves, Serbs, Croats, a large number of men there. This was no problem at all. If they were good at their jobs, well, why not let them go ahead with it. There would be nothing objectionable about that, would it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: The reference here is to the civilian bodies believing that the Division was merely a burden for Zavidovici Municipality. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do believe that it was true. You could feel this in a thousand different ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: They made requests that they should use their own personnel to fill certain positions, such as assistant commander for Morale, Logistics, Security and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: They were adamant that persons of suspicious moral qualities should be appointed, even people with criminal records; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: They drove certain commanders to resign, Lajid Hasanagic, for example, and so on and so forth well?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that and many other things as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You saw references here to the Asim Camdzic unit, the unit that I asked you about a while ago, and the El Mujahedin unit. Is it true that the civilian bodies praised and even aggrandized the roles of these units, the El Mujahedin Detachment and the Asim Camdzic unit and this type of unit, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's true. If you look at the report, you see the assistant commander for Morale passing this off as the commander's report. I think that speaks for itself, doesn't it? It sort of puts you in the picture and very much corroborates what you are suggesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: At the same time, the civilian bodies were creating this atmosphere of distrust towards the army commands, and they exaggerated the importance of the Mujahedin and the Asim Camdzic unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can I please ask you to, just for a minute, look at page 2 of this document? Page 3 of the English. And I'm asking you to look at the second sentence right at the beginning of the text in Bosnian, where it says -- Your Honours, well, now it's been scrolled down. Could you please stop it right there? There, where it says "the fact that the commander ...," that would be line 6 or 7 in the English version. And, Witness, I'm asking you whether you agree that -- whether it says here that the fact that among the good officers in the unit who obey are the commander of the Mujahedin unit, the Asim Camdzic? It seems that such units obey the civilian authorities, not the military authorities. Would you agree with me, on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Was this, in fact, how it was in reality?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "approximately"?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean approximately, that's how it was, more or less. Perhaps it was even worse than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And could you perhaps --

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I mean to say that this influence over those people who commanded such units was even stronger. The politicians had even stronger influence than the way you painted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm talking on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm telling you on the basis of my feelings and on the basis of what I was able to observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yet on the basis of what you say, I conclude that the influence of the local politicians in Zavidovici was especially strong over this type of units, the Mujahedin and the Asim Camdzic unit. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Fine. Now I would like to ask you to look at another part of this document. That's the fifth paragraph that's in Bosnian and second paragraph on page 4 of the English version, Your Honours. And now I would like you to look at a portion of this paragraph, where it says the power cuts and the fact that the telephones are no longer functioning during combat operations is a problem that needs to be investigated further. This is addressed to the 35th Division commander and the Zavidovici post office. That's a civilian organisation. Is it possible that the relations were so strained that the civilian authorities cut off power during combat operations; is that the fact?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall that particular instance, but there were such situations quite often. I don't recall this particular case, but there were situations where we faced a thousand and one problems because the civilian authorities did not want to do what we'd asked them to do. This was something that we had a right to, not something that we just asked them to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: This is a document from the 12th of August. Is this -- do you recall whether there were any power cuts or whether telephone lines were cut in July, in combat operations in July 1995? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, I remember I wanted to believe that those cuts were the result of something else, some defects, but this is true, what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you. We see from this document that the El Mudjahedin Detachment is mentioned. The Prosecutor asked you some questions today, and now I want to ask you some questions about this detachment. Could we please put this document away. On the basis of your evidence today and on the basis of what you said while you were interviewed by the OTP in a very leading manner, very insistent manner, you said that you had very little knowledge of Arabs, including the El Mudjahedin Detachment. And now I want to show you what you said about the El Mujahedin. I'm referring now to tape 9393A, page 3 in Bosnian, both in Bosnian and in English versions. That's the interview with the investigators. You spoke about the Mujahedin, and you said at that time: "I started to get a picture, a general picture, about, conditionally speaking, their lack of organisation, or rather not of their organisation but of their way of life and their way of operating, and I was sure then that they were divided into two or more levels. One of those levels that was in contact with the people, with the Bosnians, people in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I think that those were people from the secular part and their only duty was for all those contacts, talks, getting closer, and all the other elements, those elements were hidden from the eye of the other people, they were illusive." So what you told the OTP investigators, was that the way that you saw the Arabs that you saw moving around the Zavidovici area?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You were the intelligence officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I believe that regardless of what you tell us today, that you tried, with all your might, to get as much information as possible about them.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But you could not do so. Those were closed units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: They were illusive; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: On the basis of that, I conclude that for you and the division, it was virtually impossible to identify those Arabs.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: You can skip the "virtual" parts. It was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: The fact that you did not have much data about the El Mudjahedin Detachment, that was the reflection of the actual situation on the ground and the contacts with that unit on the ground?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like the witness to look at a document. That would be Exhibit 428.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Witness, this is a 3rd Corps document, as you can see. It concerns the Manuvar-94. The date is the 24th of October, and the participation of the El Mudjahedin Detachment is mentioned here. They were supposed to participate together with the OG Bosna. You were in the OG Bosna Command at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes -- probably, yes. Yes, yes, for sure, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: On the basis of your evidence today, I conclude that you did not know about the resubordination of this unit, or rather that you did not understand that this unit was now operating as part of the 35th Division; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And the reason for that is the fact that this unit did not act as a unit, subordinate -- resubordinated to the 35th Division; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: They did not attend the briefings in the 35th Division, or at least not regularly? When I say that, I don't mean visits to the Division. I am talking about the briefings, where you discussed things. I don't know if you know about that.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: They did not attend any of the briefings where I was, and I'm sure that I attended all the regular briefings. No Arabs were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: They did not submit combat reports?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say whether they submitted them to anyone, but I myself did not know about them. I did not know about any combat reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Division.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Division. I never saw any such report or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please put this document away. And since I still have some more time, I would now -- I would now like the witness to look at E396, a document that was shown to him by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does "E" in the 396 stand for "Exhibit" or is it just --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit, Your Honour, yes. It's an exhibit, Your Honour, 396.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Do you remember that the Prosecutor showed you this report today?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Could you please look at it. Again we're talking about the resubordination of the El Mudjahedin Detachment, for the purpose of some major tasks relating to difficult elevations, and the way I understand this document, the El Mujahedin should carry out the reconnaissance of these areas indicated here. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you the following: You are an intelligence officer. You are the assistant commander for Intelligence. You would be the person who would receive any reconnaissance reports, because these would be reports that were the result of a reconnaissance of enemy positions; am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You never received any reports of this kind from them?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Simply put, they did not submit any intelligence to you? When I say "you," I mean the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: They did not. I would have known if any such reports had come in in any part of the 35th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: They did not submit any security information?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't think they did, but I don't want to get tangled up in other people's sectors. I did not have anything to do with security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, that's fair enough. But no intelligence?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I never received any intelligence from them, and I never saw any such thing in the Division at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And I am right if I believe that under the rules, you were to have an intelligence officer in every subordinate unit, in every subordinate unit, battalion, detachment, whatever; you would be in contact with that officer, and you would issue instructions to him, and he would give you feedback? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Did you have any officers that you could contact, whom you could instruct and from whom you could get feedback there?

utterances.speaker: IZUDIN HAJDERHODZIC
utterances.text: I didn't know anyone, intelligence officers or anybody else from the El Mudjahedin Detachment. I literally didn't know anyone. The only person that I saw was the Emir. That was that one time, but that was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, thank you. Your Honours, I would stop my cross-examination at this point because I believe our time is up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. We'll take an adjournment and come back tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, sir, in the same courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
